description:
A figure per field placing the measured permanent zero fraction beside the measured determinant zero fraction computed on the same drawn matrices, with the exact finite-size singular probability overlaid.

## Background

The contrast is the point of the whole question. The determinant's zero probability is pinned exactly at every finite size by $1 - \prod_{i=1}^{n}(1 - q^{-i})$ and tends to a limit around $0.4399$ at $q = 3$, while the permanent's is conjectured to tend to $1/q$ — for $q = 3$ a separation between roughly $0.44$ and $0.33$ that a single figure makes visible in a way a table does not.

Two framings must not be confused. This figure compares zero fractions, which is what the campaign measures; a whole-distribution uniformity comparison between permanent and determinant values is a different question belonging to separate prior work in this repository.

The determinant curve is drawn against its exact finite-size values rather than its limit, since the limit overstates the exact value by more than a campaign standard error at the smallest sizes.

## Success Criteria

- [aspirational] REQ-01: A figure per field plots the measured $\Pr[\mathrm{per}(A) = 0]$ and $\Pr[\det(A) = 0]$ against $n$, both with interval error bars, from the counts the campaign recorded on the same drawn matrices.
- [aspirational] REQ-02: The exact finite-size singular probability $1 - \prod_{i=1}^{n}(1 - q^{-i})$ is overlaid, and any asymptotic limit shown is drawn as a distinct asymptote that no measured point is compared against.
- [aspirational] REQ-03: The figure is generated from the finalized dataset by the committed analysis pipeline, with no hand-entered value.
- [aspirational] REQ-04: The caption states the sample count per point and the interval level.
- [aspirational] REQ-05: Cells where the campaign ran without the determinant companion are absent from the determinant series rather than shown as zero.
- [aspirational] REQ-06: The figure and its caption present a zero-fraction comparison, distinct from a whole-distribution uniformity comparison.

## Notes

Every criterion here is aspirational: the figure's value depends on the cells the campaign completes for both quantities. It is a derived artefact and sits outside the dataset's raw checksum set.
title: Permanental against determinantal zero-fraction comparison figure
